archetypes.name: Azorius Scry-Surveil Tempo
archetypes.plan: Chain cheap scry/surveil effects to grow Diviner of Victory-style payoffs and enable Jace planeswalkers, while tapping down blockers with stun effects and flying attackers close the game.

archetypes.name: Orzhov Removal & Recursion Midrange
archetypes.plan: Win by out-removing the opponent with efficient black/white kill spells and life gain, then recurring key creatures (Rewrite Regrets, Generous Revival) to grind out value while premium rares like Garruk close.

archetypes.name: Boros Aggro-Empower
archetypes.plan: Win with cheap aggressive red-white creatures backed by efficient removal and combat tricks; wide boards turn Repurposed Enforcer and Master of Barbs into game-ending engines while premium spot removal clears blockers.

archetypes.name: Selesnya Lifegain Counters
archetypes.plan: Gain life repeatedly through cheap lifelink/lifegain sources and convert it into +1/+1 counters and card advantage with Bloombrute, Lyra, and Unflinching Hortimancer, outscaling opponents in board stalls.

archetypes.name: Dimir Threshold Mill
archetypes.plan: Fill your graveyard with cheap mills and surveil to hit seven cards, then deploy threshold payoffs like Null Summoner and Void Extrapolator while recursive spells such as Recursive Recruitment and Rewrite Regrets grind out value behind removal.

archetypes.name: Izzet Spells & Jace Empowerment
archetypes.plan: Cast lots of cheap instants/sorceries to grow prowess creatures and empower Jace planeswalkers, which generate card advantage and burn while prowess fliers close the game.

archetypes.name: Simic Ramp-and-Empower
archetypes.plan: Ramp early with land-fetch elves and mana dorks into huge green finishers like Verdant Kraken and Hungering Puppetbeast, while cheap 'empower Jace' triggers (Arcane Amphisbaena, Mindseeker Oculus) fuel planeswalkers that protect the board and generate value until the fatties close.

archetypes.name: Rakdos Noncombat Damage / Discard
archetypes.plan: Win by grinding opponents down with incidental noncombat damage from discard and sacrifice effects while pumping your team (Master of Barbs) and recurring threats like Grim Repriser; removal like Break Under Pressure and Multiply by Zero clears blockers so evasive prepared creatures close the game.

archetypes.name: Golgari Graveyard Threshold
archetypes.plan: Mill your own library early with cheap enablers to hit seven cards in the graveyard for Threshold payoffs and big-mana recursion, while premium black removal and deathtouch bodies hold the board until large threats close the game.

archetypes.name: Gruul Heartwood Ramp
archetypes.plan: Ramp out huge artifact-creature payoffs (Hungering Puppetbeast, Craftwork Crusher, Verdant Kraken) using Heartwood tokens and land-fetch enablers, then smash through with trample while burn spells clear blockers.

mechanics.name: Empower Jace / planeswalkers
mechanics.summary: Many spells 'Empower Jace X' to add loyalty counters to a Jace planeswalker; cards like Sanctum Lurker, Rewrite Regrets and Protege's Awakening feed it, and 'Way of' enchantments give planeswalkers extra abilities. Prioritize early planeswalkers and beholding them.

mechanics.name: Prepared
mechanics.summary: Creatures enter or become prepared via various triggers (Stingerquill Voxmancer, Woodwork Prodigy) and prepared status gates stronger effects; Hexhaven Dueling Arena can prepare attackers.

mechanics.name: Threshold & graveyard fill
mechanics.summary: Self-mill (Dark Matter Manipulator, Something Worth Saving, Theorix Charm) enables seven-card Threshold payoffs like Void Extrapolator and Proft, Sinister Mastermind plus recursion such as Recursive Recruitment.

mechanics.name: Scry/surveil matters
mechanics.summary: Consider, Diviner of Victory, Proft Consulting Detective and Denzilore Fatehold reward repeated scrying/surveiling with pumps and card advantage.

mechanics.name: Life gain payoffs
mechanics.summary: White-green builds life-gain engines (Lyra Archangel of Dawn, Bloombrute, Germinate Recruits creating Cadets off life gained); solid but weaker than blue shells.

mechanics.name: Big-ramp green
mechanics.summary: Verdant Kraken tokens, Simulacrum Shaper ramp and discounted giants (Ghalta variants) power Gruul's mid-size beatdown plan.

primer.overview: FRAGMENTS OF THE ECHOVERSE is a planeswalker-centric format built around 'Empower Jace', the 'prepared' mechanic, and heavy self-mill/threshold payoffs. Blue-based decks dominate (Azorius 57.9%, Dimir 56.9%) alongside aggressive Gruul ramp; premium removal and planeswalkers carry decks while weak color pairs like Simic and Orzhov should be avoided.
pick_principles: Take rare/mythic planeswalkers extremely early — Garruk Veiled Butcher (+16.1 IWD), Ajani Unrelenting (+18.1) and The Theorist Jace (+16.6) are format-warping.
Draft premium interaction highly: Break Under Pressure (+7.7 IWD), Multiply by Zero (+5.9) and Extended Absence (+5.1) answer the format's big threats cheaply.
Commit to blue-white or blue-black early — they're the clear top pairs; avoid Simic and Orzhov lanes.
Secure an early Jace planeswalker before loading up on Empower payoffs — the payoffs need the walker to function.
In black decks, mill enablers feeding Threshold (Void Extrapolator) and recursion (Theoretical Necromancer) form a real engine.
Pick efficient stat-sticks with upside early: Sphinx of False Conclusions (+11.3 IWD) and Mindseeker Oculus (+7.3) outperform their slot.
Gruul wants ramp into oversized bodies — Verdant Kraken (+6.6 IWD) and Craftwork Crusher (+9.7) anchor it.
Two-land-check duals (Deserted Beach cycle) fix mana smoothly; grab them mid-draft over marginal playables.

synergy_notes.why: Every surveil triggers Diviner's +1/+1 pump, turning a 1-mana cantrip into repeated combat growth.
Proctor surveils on creature entry, enabling both its own recursion (requires having scried/surveilled) and payoffs like Denizlore Fatehold.
Charm's draw mode empowers Jace while its +1/+2 mode stacks with Futurescribe's surveil-boosted combat pump.
Oculus empowers Jace 4 on entry, accelerating toward Jace's high-value ultimate and loyalty draws.
Four copies of Approach in the graveyard let you tutor out the Sphinx, whose death creates a copying token.
Reanimating Apex Witchstalker re-triggers its enter-the-battlefield life gain and gives a menace body; its basic landcycling also fills the graveyard so Rewrite Regrets always has a target.
Returning Blessed Ghoul with a +1/+1 counter gives a cheap lifelink attacker that can later be recurred from the graveyard for repeated value.
Sacrificing a redundant creature as Silence the Echo's cost turns removal into card advantage when the sacrificed creature is recoverable via Theoretical Necromancer's exile-from-graveyard ability.
Stacked removal lets you answer both the biggest threat (highest-mana-value sacrifice) and any follow-up threat with exile, keeping the board clear for your recursive creatures.
Every opposing creature killed by Last Gasp never enters again, denying Gideon's punish triggers to the opponent while your removal keeps their board empty for Gideon's ward to protect.
Landcycling and self-sacrifice effects fill your graveyard quickly so Void Extrapolator reliably hits threshold and becomes a 3/3 for two mana.

Hexhaven Battalion creates three Cadet tokens and Empower Jace 2; with four-plus creatures attacking, Repurposed Enforcer triggers for large Jace empowerment each attack, stacking loyalty rewards on a cheap body.
Every noncombat damage event from burn like No Admittance pumps your whole team +1/+0 for the turn, turning cheap removal into a combat-phase power spike.
Tomik upgrades all your noncombat damage by 1, so Fulminous Forte's mode dealing 1 to each opposing creature and planeswalker sweeps x+1 damage across their board.
Samut gives all creatures haste so Skilled Battlecarver can attack immediately and pump with its {1}{R} activation the same turn it enters.
Each noncreature spell you cast pumps your whole team; cheap instants/sorceries like Surgical Precision convert spell density into extra combat damage through Convoke-fueled turns.
Guiding Hydra is an early pick (ALSA 1.6) that trades counters for card advantage; Generous Revival returns it from the graveyard with an extra +1/+1 counter to re-run the engine.
Propagator gains 1 life for every other creature entering, reliably turning on Bloombrute's once-per-turn draw-a-card lifegain trigger.
Equipping the Kitesail gives flying plus a lifegain trigger on each attack, stacking +1/+1 counters on the Hortimancer every combat.
Each mode of Surgical Precision gains life (1 or 2), feeding Titanbones two +1/+1 counters per lifegain event despite its low baseline.
Repeated landfall lifegain from Koth puts a +1/+1 counter on Lyra each time a land enters, quickly making her a game-ending flier.
The draw-and-gain-3-life mode both replaces itself and triggers Bloombrute's card draw; the fight mode also protects your board.
Returning a small creature with an added +1/+1 counter re-triggers enter-the-battlefield lifegain sources like Liliana the Faultless or Greenhouse Propagator.
Mode three mills three cards toward the seven-card threshold that turns Void Extrapolator into a 3/3 body early.
Liliana mills two on every other creature entering, quickly enabling Null Summoner's threshold re-cast mode after it dies.
Both recur from your own graveyard; Recursive Recruitment cast back from the graveyard makes buffed Cadets scaled to graveyard size.
Manipulator mills three on entry and gains +2/+0 per seven cards in your graveyard, so repeated milling grows it to a 5/0-plus attacker.
Uldaros copies and casts spells exiled from your graveyard on entry; Rewrite Regrets returns him (MV 6) from the graveyard to repeat the effect.
Yuriko's surveil 2 mode fills the graveyard toward the seven cards Loot needs to activate its sacrifice ability.
Flashback/casting spells off the graveyard still triggers prowess and grows Variable Chaser; Twinned Vision draws two when not cast from hand, fueling more spells.
Both are pure 'empower Jace' enablers — each cast pumps a Jace planeswalker toward ultimate-level loyalty abilities while Oculus also blocks as a body.
Beholding Jace lets Countersculpt skip its extra mana, and empowered Jaces convert every cheap spell into loyalty value.
Discarding nonland cards to Seasoned Cryomancer taps down multiple attackers and feeds Twinned Vision's flashback from the graveyard.
Every point of noncombat damage from empowered-Jace burn effects gets amplified by +1 through Tomik's replacement effect.
Each first noncreature spell empowers Jace 1, stacking with Jace's Machinations' empower 8 to reach big loyalty abilities quickly and activate them at instant speed.
Shaper fetches an extra basic land onto the battlefield early, accelerating you by a full turn toward casting the 7-mana Kraken, whose upkeep tokens take over the ground game.
Both commons carry 'empower Jace' on entry, so a cheap deathtouch body and a 3-drop Homunculus each pump your Jace planeswalker several loyalty steps ahead of schedule for free.

Cultivator returns lands from graveyard to hand to keep ramping; Something Worth Saving mills four and lets you retrieve a permanent — either refueling Cultivator's recursion targets or grabbing a fatty.

Puppetbeast creates a Heartwood token on entry and grows by sacrificing artifacts; Heartwood Crafter makes spare colorless mana that can't cast spells from hand but perfectly funds the {1} sac-activation pumps.
Cheap instants that each empower Jace multiple loyalty counters, turning low-cost interaction into massive planeswalker acceleration before landing your finishers.

Activate a planeswalker loyalty ability (e.g., via empowered Jace), then attack with Kiora to untap an attacker and make it unblockable — Tam's Resistance adds vigilance/counters so the same creature swings profitably every turn.
Vitriol deals 2 noncombat damage and forces a discard; both halves trigger Tinybones' ping, stacking repeated damage each turn.
Forced discard counts as noncombat damage to opponents via Tomik-boosted sources; Master of Barbs pumps your whole team whenever the discard package fires.
Rank Rat's ETB discard triggers Tinybones' damage immediately and fills the graveyard toward threshold for Void Extrapolator.
Once you've dealt noncombat damage this turn (Vitriol, Soulbreaker, Tinybones), Repriser returns from the graveyard with prowess already online—a free recursive threat.
Soulbreaker's attack trigger deals noncombat damage to each opponent, turning on Wordsmith's flying and haste permanently after one attack.
Tomik adds +1 to every noncombat damage source you control; Charm's 3-damage mode becomes 4 and every Tinybones/Soulbreaker ping grows by one.
Primal Witchstalker mills four on entry, pushing you toward the seven-card graveyard count that gives Void Extrapolator its Threshold +1/+1.
Manipulator mills three on entry and grows +2/+0 per seven cards in your graveyard; Something Worth Saving mills four more and lets you keep a permanent card, compounding both the buff and Threshold.
The mill fills your graveyard so Rewrite Regrets can reanimate a MV6-or-less creature or planeswalker late as a two-for-one threat.
Liliana mills two per creature you control to feed Threshold fast, and her Exhaust ability returns a graveyard creature — the same yard Rewrite Regrets recurs.
Hapatra's ETB puts -1/-1 counters equal to the greatest MV in your graveyard; milling high-MV cards with Primal Witchstalker makes her entry removal much stronger.

Both use the graveyard as a resource: Gallia exiles a creature card to recur herself with a counter, and Theoretical Necromancer exiles itself to return another creature to hand, extending the mill plan into card advantage.

Tethermage sacrifices a land to make two tapped Heartwood artifact tokens; those artifacts both discount nothing directly but feed Puppetbeast's {1}, sacrifice another artifact activation for +1/+1 counters and also give it bodies to sac, while Puppetbeast itself creates a Heartwood token on entry t
Shaper ramps a basic land onto the battlefield early, accelerating you toward casting the 7-mana Verdant Kraken, whose upkeep 3/3 land-creature tokens then provide further lands and board presence.
Cultivator returns land cards from graveyard to hand on combat damage, refueling the land-sacrifice/ramp plan so you can afford the 7-mana Craftwork Crusher and still hold interaction.

Aerid creates Heartwood artifact tokens on entry and death and pumps off artifacts you control; those same artifacts fuel Puppetbeast's sacrifice activations, so one legend powers both the pump and the counter engine.

Cheap red removal clears blockers so your big tramplers connect; Violent Echoes' 6 damage doubles as removal and empowers Jace when it overkills, adding planeswalker pressure on top of the beatdown plan.

Kiora makes 5/5 Dragon tokens immediately and repeatedly via her {8} ability; each Dragon is an artifact-free large body that Craterclaw Colossus buffs with trample and +X/+0 based on your artifact count for a lethal swing.

traps.why: -9.3 IWD and worst-in-set performance despite looking like flexible pump — pure filler.
-4.1 IWD; slow artifact that mills yourself toward a weak payoff rather than advancing the board.
-3.9 IWD; conditional graveyard return requires opponent damage first and rarely lines up.
-3.9 IWD; needs a dedicated life-gain engine that most decks lack.
-3.0 IWD; counter-amplification payoff with no reliable counter sources in white.
-3.5 IWD; looting body that trades poorly in a format decided by bigger swings.
-3.8 IWD; low-impact combat trick that Boros's mediocre win rate can't support.
-1.6 IWD; aura deathtouch grant is easily blanked by the format's plentiful removal.
